source_documents.title: Steric Control of Molecular Packing Governs Excimer Emission in Fluorene-Based Molecular Solids

reference_evidence_units.quote: Consistent with this assignment, minimal solvatochromism is observed across solvents ranging from cyclohexane (ε′ = 2.023) to acetonitrile (ε′ = 35.94), as shown in Table S1, indicating minimal charge-transfer character.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all fluorene derivatives
reference_evidence_units.statement: Minimal solvatochromism: emission is from a locally excited fluorene state, not charge transfer.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, none of the tert-butyl-substituted derivatives exhibit rise-time components, indicating that excimer formation is not established under these packing conditions.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2-tbF, 2,7-dtbF, 3,6-dtbF
reference_evidence_units.statement: tert-Butyl derivatives show no excimer formation; emission stays monomer-like.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This clear decoupling demonstrates that the red-shifted emission observed in the solid state does not originate from triplet-state phosphorescence.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all fluorene derivatives
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 77 K phosphorescence vs room-temperature solid emission
reference_evidence_units.statement: The solid-state long-wavelength emission is not phosphorescence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Triplet emission exists at 77 K but is not the solid-state emission studied.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Conversely, 3,6-dtbF exhibits consistently low ϕF values (∼0.07) despite similar lifetimes, indicating that steric congestion suppresses both efficient excimer formation and radiative recombination by preventing favorable π–π overlap and promoting nonradiative decay (Figure S4).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 3,6-dtbF
reference_evidence_units.statement: Low solid-state quantum yield of 3,6-dtbF at similar lifetime is attributed to suppressed radiative recombination and enhanced nonradiative decay.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Interpretation of yield and lifetime; the rate constants are in Table S2.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Low solid-state yield explained by suppressed radiative recombination and enhanced nonradiative decay.

environment_context.effect: tert-butyl groups prevent cofacial pi-stacking in the crystal

contrast_group.factor: steric bulk of 2,7/3,6 alkyl substituents (methyl vs tert-butyl)
contrast_group.difference: methyl/unsubstituted pack cofacially and form excimers; tert-butyl disrupts stacking and suppresses excimers
